# [EPIC] Backlog audit: every artifact Scrum-shaped, true to the code, proven by tests

## Epic
Bring every issue on this board to one standard:

1. It matches its issue template.
2. It is written to the repo writing standard.
3. Its claims match the code as it is now.
4. Every acceptance criterion names a test or command that proves it.

Scope: 12 epics, 38 stories and 136 tasks that predate this epic, plus the
12 bugs and 4 untyped issues.

Structure. One Story per epic under audit. Under each, one Task per story
under that epic, and that Task's acceptance criteria name every task under
that story individually. Nothing is audited as a group, so nothing is
skipped. #311 holds template and tooling maintenance and stays open for the
life of the epic.

Findings that set the standard, from the audit of epic #1:

- #3, #4 and #5 each closed on a dated criterion ("verified 2025-11-14")
  with no test behind it.
- #2 named `frontend/filmpire`. ADR-013 renamed that directory to
  `frontend/lmdb`.
- #2 to #5 carried a `sprint-0` label while their milestone was Sprint 1.
- Story #83 had one acceptance criterion covering four tasks.
- #77 was closed with its child task #120 still open.

#109 and #250 were both defects in work whose issues were closed and green.

## Business Value
Closing an issue without proof removes it from review, so nobody re-checks
it. If each criterion names a test, CI fails when the behaviour breaks.
Without a test, the break is not detected.

## Product Goal alignment
Indirect. This epic ships no product feature. The backlog is where features
are specified and accepted, so incorrect issues propagate into what gets
built from them.

## Notes
The four gates (Shape, Voice, Truth, Proof) and the writing standard are in
`.claude/skills/audit-artifacts/`.

Epic #1 is done: 6 issues, 4 dated criteria replaced by `ProjectStructureTest`
in shared-library, which Backend CI runs.

Bugs sit outside the epic hierarchy, so #312 audits all 13 of them. #316
audits the 10 tasks that belong to no story. Between the 12 epic stories,
#311, #312 and #316, every issue on the board is covered.
